parts.title: Summary
parts.author: Request or handoff author
parts.reviewer: Authoring-side owner. If a reply changes the status, the team owning that fact also confirms it
parts.review_check: Do the problem, required answer, settled and open matters, and next action match the state in the body?
parts.narrative_role: Helps the reader identify the problem and the judgment needed at the start.

parts.title: Document identity and status
parts.author: Document owner
parts.reviewer: Document owner and the people who can confirm each status
parts.review_check: Do not turn missing owner information into an assertion that no owner is assigned. Use unassigned only when nonassignment is confirmed. Are the current author, scope, version and status clear? Are previous documents and document IDs linked only when they exist?
parts.narrative_role: Places the document details at the end.

parts.title: Evidence notes
parts.requirement: Conditionally required when actual material is cited. Omit when there is none; existing documents are not required
parts.author: Observer or investigator
parts.reviewer: An owner on the responsible team with access to the code, operations or screen for each fact
parts.review_check: Is the scope confirmed by direct observations, code, captures, logs and measurement records accurate? Do notes connect to actual citations without assuming unavailable material or past documents?
parts.narrative_role: Places the sources, original material and limitations of body notes at the end.

parts.title: Problem and desired outcome
parts.requirement: Required for additions/changes, bugs, removal/migration and performance requests. Optional for fact questions and handoffs
parts.author: The side that observed the problem
parts.reviewer: Owner on the observing team. If expected behavior is product policy, the person responsible for that decision
parts.review_check: Are observations and expectations specific? Has the impact been overstated as though its full extent had been checked?
parts.narrative_role: Explains the need through the situation and the gap between actual and expected behavior.

parts.title: Requests and questions
parts.author: Request or handoff author
parts.reviewer: The sender confirms the required result; the recipient confirms the question, scope and acceptance of responsibility directed to them
parts.review_check: Are requests, questions and implementation proposals distinguished? Will the answer determine the requesting side’s next action?
parts.narrative_role: Connects the preceding explanation to the judgment needed from the other side and follow-up action.

parts.title: Causes and hypotheses
parts.requirement: Required for bug investigations. A confirmed cause is not required; an unknown cause is allowed. Optional for other types
parts.author: Investigator
parts.reviewer: Owner on the team responsible for the relevant code, data or operational path
parts.review_check: Are observed symptoms separated from causal inference? Is there a way to confirm or reject the hypothesis?
parts.narrative_role: Explains which interpretation the observations support and what remains unconfirmed.

parts.title: External behavior contract
parts.requirement: Required for additions/changes, removal/migration and implementation handoffs. Required for bugs and performance work if external behavior changes
parts.author: Proposing side and provider
parts.reviewer: The provider checks guarantees and meaning; the consumer checks actual dependencies. The relevant decision owner handles policy judgments only
parts.review_check: Are required results separated from internal implementation? Are null, permission, aggregation and exception semantics sufficiently explained?
parts.narrative_role: Explains the external behavior that addresses the problem.

parts.title: Implementation options
parts.requirement: Optional for all types. Use when proposing an internal approach
parts.author: Proposer
parts.reviewer: The implementation-owning team decides the method. Other teams confirm only conditions affecting shared contracts, cost or schedule
parts.review_check: Has an attractive implementation been treated as an obligation for the other side? Are assumptions, measurements and estimated costs distinguished?
parts.narrative_role: Explains differences between approaches to obtaining the required result.

parts.title: Impact and migration
parts.requirement: Required for additions/changes and removal/migration. Also required for other types if consumer migration, existing data changes or removal are affected
parts.author: Change owners on both sides
parts.reviewer: Each affected consumer and provider owner. The relevant operations owner if deployment or data changes are involved
parts.review_check: Has global removal been decided based only on one’s own consumer? Are migration, removal and recovery conditions recorded, along with actual acceptance of responsibility?
parts.narrative_role: Explains how the change affects other consumers and migration.

parts.title: Acceptance criteria and verification plan
parts.requirement: Required for changes, bugs, removal, performance and handoffs. A short fact question may close with the answer required in P05
parts.author: The side defining the required result and the side performing verification
parts.reviewer: Both sides confirm shared results and conditions; the executor confirms the feasible scope
parts.review_check: Are expected results observable? Have unagreed criteria been treated as pass conditions? Are plans separated from execution?
parts.narrative_role: Closes with what to verify and what to do next.

parts.title: Owning team reply
parts.requirement: Required when writing an actual reply. Do not prefill in the initial request
parts.author: Owner of the area being asked about
parts.reviewer: The actual owner who can confirm code, operational or policy facts in that area
parts.review_check: Does the reply answer the question directly and separate confirmed scope, unknowns and constraints in its own area? Does it avoid requiring tracking IDs or past documents to answer?
parts.narrative_role: Updates current understanding and remaining questions with the new answer.

parts.title: Decisions and corrections
parts.requirement: Required when deciding a shared contract or policy, or correcting existing facts or agreements
parts.author: Document owner and the relevant decision owner
parts.reviewer: Both provider and consumer for shared contracts. The relevant decision maker for product, permission or operational policies. The owning team for technical fact corrections
parts.review_check: Is there an actual choice or confirmation record? Are corrections and comparisons recorded only when there is previous content to change?
parts.narrative_role: Records detailed decision and correction history at the end.

parts.title: Implementation handoff and executed verification
parts.requirement: Required at implementation handoff or closure. In an initial request, write plans only; do not fill this Part as executed results
parts.author: Implementation owner and verification executor
parts.reviewer: The provider checks implementation, environment and evidence; the consumer checks its own integration and migration results. Operations confirms only necessary deployment and data scope
parts.review_check: Can implementation and integration conditions be understood from this document alone? Are verification and deployment stated within the actually confirmed scope, with comparison to prior agreement only when differences exist?
parts.narrative_role: Explains the implementation scope and the meaning of actual confirmation results.

parts.title: Human review record
parts.requirement: Required for all types. At drafting, record planned reviewer roles only and keep pending review until actual confirmation
parts.author: Each actual reviewer. The document owner compiles the record accurately
parts.reviewer: Record only the scope actually confirmed by the reviewer. Do not infer another person’s approval or review
parts.review_check: Describe planned review by role, key scope and body location without explaining all conditions again. Missing past records leave review occurrence unconfirmed. Are the actual person, section or question to check, document version, time and remaining conditions connected? Can the review scope be found without task tracking IDs?
parts.narrative_role: Tracks the scope of actual human confirmation at the end.

parts.title: Visual material
parts.requirement: Conditionally required when judgment depends on seeing a screen or behavior. If capture is unavailable, record the missing attachment and who should confirm it
parts.author: Observer or person explaining the flow
parts.reviewer: The observing team for actual screens; the team owning each step for relationships and sequence
parts.review_check: Are actual captures, originals, annotated copies and explanatory diagrams distinguished, and problem locations clearly marked with borders and numbers? Are GIF reproduction order, static alternatives, sensitive information and inclusion appropriate?
parts.narrative_role: Places original captures, full responses and attached diagrams at the end.

parts.title: Performance and scale
parts.requirement: Required for performance requests. Also required for other types when measurements determine adoption of an option or completion
parts.author: Person able to measure and proposer of the result
parts.reviewer: The executor confirms measurement and interpretation; the consumer confirms required user outcomes and acceptance criteria
parts.review_check: Are local and production, measured and expected, and single-run and distribution figures distinguished? Are correctness, cost and sample conditions included?
parts.narrative_role: Explains the key figures and interpretation needed for performance judgments.

parts.title: Asynchronous processing and state
parts.requirement: Required when newly defining or changing acceptance, completion, failure, retry, cancellation or notification behavior
parts.author: Owner of each step
parts.reviewer: Each step’s owning team confirms its processing and signals; the consuming team confirms user-visible states and recovery flow
parts.review_check: Are successful HTTP responses separated from processing completion? Are ID granularity, retry responsibility, idempotency and missed events on reconnection apparent?
parts.narrative_role: Explains actors, states, and the sequence of failure and recovery.

parts.title: Permissions and policy
parts.requirement: Required when changing authentication, authorization or exposure policy, or when a policy judgment is needed
parts.author: Team owning the behavior and policy proposer
parts.reviewer: The provider confirms enforcement, the consumer confirms screen and feature meaning, and the relevant policy owner confirms policy choices only
parts.review_check: Are current code, desired policy and deployment configuration distinguished? Has success under specific conditions been expanded into overall safety or completed verification?
parts.narrative_role: Explains the permissions and policies users will rely on and the judgments still needed.
